program.tuple: <Sigma, Q, q_0, delta, F, M, A, E_P>
program.note: Abstract state space Q may be non-computable; practical SBG uses finite trace approximations

genome_extraction.formula: Phi(P, I) = A({ phi(tau(P,i)) : i ~ mu_I, i in S })

behavioral_distance.aggregation: weighted L^p with default p=1, uniform weights

semantic_equivalence.operational_approximation: P1 ≡_S^epsilon P2 iff D(G(P1), G(P2)) < epsilon
semantic_equivalence.undecidability_note: Full semantic equivalence is undecidable by Rice's theorem; SBG computes empirical approximation only

key_assumptions.statement: Environment is stable (fixed) during any single execution
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Trace events are not reproducible; genome extraction is undefined

key_assumptions.statement: Version identity (which versions constitute the same program) is supplied externally
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Longitudinal genome comparison (H4) has no defined object to compare

key_assumptions.statement: Inputs drawn from I are mutually independent
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Sample aggregation formula in Definition 21 is biased; requires session-state modeling
Probability measure mu_I is ill-defined; statistical convergence arguments fail

key_assumptions.statement: All execution traces are finite (divergent executions excluded via timeout T_max)
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Genome extraction is undefined for non-terminating programs; timeout introduces truncation bias

key_assumptions.statement: Execution is deterministic given fixed input and environment; non-determinism requires canonical policy (fixed seed, serialized scheduling)
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Multiple traces for the same input produce different genome components; aggregation conflates non-determinism with behavioral variance

key_assumptions.statement: Sample size N is sufficient for distributional convergence of genome features
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: Estimated genome G_N deviates from population genome G_inf; false positive/negative regression detections increase

key_assumptions.statement: Chosen heap abstraction Q_abs is sufficiently expressive for the comparison task
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: STATE dimension cannot distinguish programs with meaningfully different memory behaviors

key_assumptions.statement: Clock resolution is sufficient that consecutive trace events have distinct timestamps
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: TEMPORAL dimension features collapse; inter-event latency distribution is degenerate

key_assumptions.statement: Location alignment map alpha covers all shared locations between program versions
key_assumptions.consequence_if_violated: CONTROL dimension distance over-estimates divergence for structurally renamed but equivalent locations

H1.name: Behavioral Genome Stability
H1.empirical_target: epsilon_stable <= 0.05 on standard benchmarks under production input distribution
dimension_caveats: TEMPORAL and RESOURCE may change under semantics-preserving optimizations

H2.name: Behavioral Genome Sensitivity
H2.formal_condition: exists i : B(P^k, i) != B(P^{k+1}, i) => D(G^k, G^{k+1}) > epsilon_detect
H2.empirical_target: statistically separable D-distributions over known-buggy vs known-equivalent version pairs (Defects4J)
H2.dependency: requires sample S to cover inputs witnessing the behavioral difference

H3.name: Cross-Language Behavioral Equivalence
H3.formal_condition: P1 ≡_S P2 across languages => D(C_E(G(P1)), C_E(G(P2))) < epsilon_xlang

H4.name: Behavioral Genome Versioning
H4.formal_condition: E[D(G^k, G^{k+1})] = O(|delta_code|^alpha) for some alpha > 0
H4.caveat: fails for non-local changes; holds in expectation over typical software change corpus

H5.name: Genome as Regression Oracle
H5.formal_condition: exists theta* : Recall(theta*) >= 0.80 and Precision(theta*) >= 0.70 on held-out corpus
dependencies: sufficient input coverage of regression-triggering inputs

H6.name: Behavioral Genome Uniqueness
H6.formal_condition: Pr[D(G(P1), G(P2)) < epsilon_collision] <= delta_collision for uniformly sampled unrelated programs
H6.caveat: trivially simple programs violate this; meaningful only over behaviorally diverse corpora

open_problems.title: Optimal Sample Size
open_problems.description: For a given program P, input distribution I, and acceptable error epsilon, what is the minimum sample size N* such that ||G_N(P) - G_inf(P)||_G <= epsilon? Unknown in general; depends on variance of behavioral features across inputs.

open_problems.title: Decidability of Operational Equivalence
open_problems.description: Is the epsilon-semantic equivalence relation ≡_S^epsilon decidable for all epsilon > 0 when restricted to finite-terminating programs? Depends on complexity of underlying genome features (GED is NP-hard).

open_problems.title: Confidence-Weighted Genome Distance
open_problems.description: Current distance D does not account for finite-sample uncertainty in genome estimation. A Welch t-statistic analog D_conf = D(G1,G2) / sqrt(sigma_G1^2 + sigma_G2^2) may yield better-calibrated regression detection.

open_problems.title: Cross-Language Procedure Alignment
open_problems.description: CONTROL dimension encodes dynamic call graphs using procedure identifiers. Cross-language comparison requires a formal mapping between procedures across language boundaries (e.g., Python sort() <-> Java Collections.sort()). No such formal mapping is defined.

open_problems.title: Heap Abstraction Selection
open_problems.description: STATE dimension is parameterized over an abstract heap domain Q_abs. A principled method for selecting the minimal-sufficient abstraction for a given comparison task is undefined.

open_problems.title: Temporal Normalization Across Architectures
open_problems.description: TEMPORAL features require normalization when comparing programs across radically different architectures (interpreted Python vs native Rust). SPECint normalization is insufficient for this case; a formal architecture-agnostic temporal equivalence metric remains open.

most_related_works.relation: INTERACTION dimension g_X extends syscall n-gram representation; SBG adds 7 further dimensions and longitudinal tracking
H1-H2 address same semantic equivalence question as regression verification, but via empirical approximation rather than formal proof
Closest in spirit: I/O semantic summaries; SBG generalizes to 8 dimensions, source-level, and longitudinal genome
Semantic diff motivation shared; SBG replaces SMT solving with execution-based approximation
